proposed_from.topic: Complete SI-PAG orientation under selection and unknown-target interventions. On finite causally sufficient DAGs in Dai et al.'s full published pre-treatment-selection interventional-twin-graph compatibility class, with observational and unknown-target soft-intervention regimes supplied as oracle regime MAGs, define the canonical SI-PAG by endpoint-mark invariance over the entire class. Give a finite sound within- and cross-regime orientation calculus whose monotone mark closure terminates after polynomially many endpoint updates, prove mark completeness by showing closure equals the canonical SI-PAG and every residual circle has two compatible orientation witnesses, and derive a complete population CDIS algorithm on the same class. Do not claim polynomial conditional-independence discovery. Use Dai et al.'s two-variable equivalence witness and sciPlex2/A549 workflow, and distinguish Jaber's no-selection theory and Luo et al.'s post-treatment-selection F-PAG.

seed_details.anchor: DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention, Introduction; Definition 1; Theorems 2--3; Section 4 completeness paragraph; Conclusion
seed_details.anchor_read: The source archive was opened. The equivalence proof removes the general discriminating-path condition using twin-MAG structure; the soundness proof invokes FCI soundness and explicitly does not construct opposing completions.
seed_details.kernel: Construct a canonical invariant-mark SI-PAG, a finite sound rule system, and a two-witness completeness theorem on the full published Dai class.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Dai's one-direction rule validation by a realizability-preserving global extension lemma for every residual endpoint.
adjacent_scan: Zhang2008CompleteFCI: single observational MAG class; supplies the endpoint-extension architecture but no regime coupling.
JaberKocaogluShanmugamBareinboim2020: unknown-target soft-intervention completeness; its tail proof excludes selection.
VenkateswaranPerkovic2026 and WangDuZhou2025: structured background knowledge and locally complete MAG rules; neither imposes common basal-world realizability.
LuoEtAl2026PostTreatmentSelection: complete post-treatment F-PAG with different timing and marks.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Zhang2008CompleteFCI because each regime is represented by a MAG.
seed_details.rebuttal: False: independently completed regime MAGs need not be projections of one basal selected DAG with a common unknown-target family.

seed_details.anchor_read: The technical report was opened. Lemma 1 realizes one oriented augmented I-MAG by a causal graph and target family; Propositions 2--3 then give opposing endpoint marks, with tail completeness relying on absence of selection bias.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize exactly when a partially oriented regime family has a common Dai twin-graph realization, with a constructive certificate or a finite obstruction.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Jaber's single-I-MAG realization must preserve one common basal DAG, selection ancestry, and ordered targets across every regime.
adjacent_scan: DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention: defines the required basal-world class but proves no converse extension lemma.
Zhang2008CompleteFCI: constructs opposing MAG completions without intervention-family realizability.
AliRichardsonSpirtes2009: characterizes MAG equivalence by ordered colliders but does not characterize projections of twin graphs.
VenkateswaranPerkovic2026: verifies restricted essential graphs in one MAG class, not a common multi-regime causal preimage.
seed_details.red_team: This is only Jaber's I-MAG realizability lemma with selection nodes added.
seed_details.rebuttal: Selection occurs in an unobserved basal world and couples inducing paths across regimes; adding ordinary MAG selection nodes does not enforce that common-world constraint.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Dai's reduction to adjacencies and v-structures fails, so ordered colliders must be synchronized across basal selection and intervention regimes.
adjacent_scan: AliRichardsonSpirtes2009: supplies the general ordered-collider equivalence theorem needed once bidirected inducing paths appear.
JaberKocaogluShanmugamBareinboim2020: supplies the latent-confounded unknown-intervention half without basal selection.

proposed_from.literature_map: The selected kernel is directly anchored to Dai et al. (ICLR 2025), whose Theorem 2 characterizes equivalence through the regime twin MAGs and whose Theorem 3 proves only soundness of CDIS. The source text explicitly leaves an equivalence-class representation and completeness open. Zhang (Artificial Intelligence 2008) proves invariant-mark completeness for one MAG Markov equivalence class. Jaber et al. (NeurIPS 2020), Definition 6, Lemma 1, and Theorem 3, give a canonical \(\Psi\)-PAG and paired endpoint witnesses for unknown-target soft interventions, but the proof excludes selection bias. Ali, Richardson, and Spirtes (Annals of Statistics 2009) supply the general ordered-collider equivalence condition. Venkateswaran and Perkovi\'c (arXiv version 4, 2026) provide restricted essential ancestral graphs and only setting-specific completeness; their discussion keeps general background-knowledge completeness open, while Wang, Du, and Zhou (ICML 2025) add locally complete rules and MAG listing. Luo et al. (ICLR 2026) prove complete F-FCI for post-treatment selection with a different F-PAG semantics. Colombo et al. (Annals of Statistics 2012) address finite-sample FCI consistency, not coupled population mark completeness. No located paper defines endpoint invariance over Dai's full basal-world compatibility class, constructs opposing globally compatible twin witnesses for every residual endpoint, or proves CDIS mark completeness on that class.
